headline: ANGLO THREATENS TO CLOSE BRAZIL NICKEL MINES IF EU BLOCKS $500M MMG SALE — DECISION DUE DECEMBER
snippet: Anglo American warned EU antitrust officials in a closed hearing today that it will likely shut its Brazilian nickel operation — which produces ferronickel critical to European stainless steel manufacturers — if regulators block the €446 million sale to MMG, the Chinese state-linked miner. The EU's preliminary objection centres on concerns MMG could divert Brazilian ferronickel away from Europe; MMG called the concerns 'fundamentally unsupported' and offered supply guarantees, with an EC decision expected by late November to December 21.

headline: BARRICK RALLIES BEFORE OPEN ON Q3 2026 BEAT — GUIDANCE REAFFIRMED AT 2.90–3.25M OZ; COPPER OUTPUT SURPRISES
snippet: Barrick Mining (TSX/NYSE: ABX) released Q3 2026 results before the market open on November 9 to a positive reception, with the stock rallying as the world's second-largest gold producer reaffirmed its full-year 2026 gold guidance of 2.90 to 3.25 million ounces alongside copper output gains from its Lumwana and Reko Diq operations. For junior gold investors, Barrick's ability to generate strong operational cash flows at $4,000+ gold validates the structural bull thesis and historically precedes valuation re-ratings cascading down to the TSX-V tier.

headline: JUNIOR MINERS DECOUPLE FROM GOLD — GDXJ SURGES 3.7% WHILE BULLION TREADS WATER ON JOBS DATA BOUNCE
snippet: FXStreet's November 9 analysis unpacks why the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) surged ~3.7% to $111.70 on a day when gold was essentially flat — the answer being that junior miners are trading as risk-on equities, rallying along with the broader stock market on the jobs data rebound rather than tracking spot gold. The implication for TSX-V investors: GDXJ's current upside is driven by equity sentiment more than gold's fundamentals — a dynamic the author views as likely corrective until gold reclaims the initiative ahead of Tuesday's CPI release.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,100 AS MARKETS WAIT — TUESDAY CPI TEST DECIDES IF DECEMBER HIKE IS A DONE DEAL
snippet: Spot gold stabilised at $4,100–$4,130 by midday November 9 — off the morning high — as traders positioned ahead of Tuesday's October CPI release with 81% of Fed futures pricing a December rate hike that could strengthen the dollar and compress gold's near-term upside. A hot print risks a test of the $4,050–$4,000 support band; a soft reading opens the path to $4,150+ as markets recalibrate the Fed outlook.

headline: UR-ENERGY Q3 — RECORD URANIUM PRODUCTION AS SHIRLEY BASIN COMES FULLY ONLINE; STOCK SLIDES DESPITE BEAT
snippet: Ur-Energy (TSX: URE / NYSE: URG) reported its strongest production quarter on record for Q3 2026, the first full period with both Lost Creek and Shirley Basin — which received Wyoming state approval in late June — running in tandem with combined licensed capacity of 4.2 million lbs U₃O₈ per year. Despite the production milestone, URE shares declined after the results, mirroring the broader uranium equity pattern of delivering operational milestones while spot prices trade below long-term contract levels where the company's deliveries are locked.

headline: FIREFLY METALS EXTENDS HIGH-GRADE COPPER-GOLD CORE ZONE LATERALLY AT GREEN BAY, NEWFOUNDLAND
snippet: FireFly Metals (ASX: FFM) released drill results on November 8 from its Green Bay Copper-Gold Project in Newfoundland showing the high-grade core zone extends further laterally than previously modelled — a continuity confirmation that underpins early-production economics. With Green Bay already carrying ~50 Mt at 2.0% CuEq Measured and Indicated, adding lateral extent to the high-grade core reduces dilution risk in the initial mining scenario that drives the project's return metrics.

headline: GOLD +4.5%, BRENT -16.4% WEEKLY — THREE COMMODITY REGIMES JUST SPLIT; GOLD MINERS BENEFIT FROM OIL'S COLLAPSE
snippet: Mitrade's November 9 weekly commodity report identifies three diverging regimes: gold extended its bull run with a 4.5% weekly gain on safe-haven and inflation-hedge demand; crude oil suffered a 16.4% weekly decline on OPEC+ supply and demand concerns; copper tracks a potential late-cycle slowdown in Chinese industrial demand. For mining investors, gold rising simultaneously with oil collapsing is structurally bullish for AISC — lower energy inputs compress costs while the gold price continues to rise, widening margins across the producer tier.

headline: SCOTIABANK: COPPER MINERS TRADING AT HISTORIC DISCOUNT TO SPOT METAL — 'RELATIVELY ATTRACTIVE' AFTER ROUT
snippet: A Scotiabank analyst published a note arguing copper mining equities have flipped from their historical premium to spot copper to an unusual discount after the sector's rout — making valuations 'relatively attractive' at current prices. The note lands as Teck Resources' Highland Valley Copper, Canada's largest open-pit mine, runs at reduced capacity in the third week of a 1,277-worker USW strike, adding a supply-side tightening signal at the precise moment copper equities are mispriced to the downside.

headline: EU TAPS CHINA'S OWN PLAYBOOK TO BREAK RARE EARTH GRIP — IEA PEGS $1.5T AT RISK FROM SUPPLY DISRUPTION
snippet: A Mining.com analysis published November 9 cites IEA data showing $1.5 trillion in EU annual economic output at risk from critical mineral supply disruptions and argues Brussels is adopting a state-backed industrial policy explicitly modelled on China's: identifying 13 strategic projects, building strategic reserves, and fast-tracking permits for domestic processing facilities including France's Carester rare earth separation plant. For TSX-V and ASX rare earth developers, the EU's declared shift to interventionist minerals policy mirrors the US DoD/DoE supply chain funding regime that has already given Energy Fuels, USA Rare Earth and others access to non-dilutive capital — a parallel European buyer market is developing.

headline: TRAILBREAKER'S MAIDEN ATSUTLA DRILL HITS 5.02 g/t Au OVER 2.30m — HIGH-GRADE TARGET DEFINED IN NW BRITISH COLUMBIA
snippet: Trailbreaker Resources (TSX-V: TBK) reported first-ever drill results from the Highlands Zone at its 100%-owned Atsutla Gold Project in northwestern British Columbia, with hole ATS-26-02 returning 5.02 g/t Au over 2.30m including 15.0 g/t Au over 0.70m in a maiden 2026 campaign. The mineralized zone was narrow where tested — typical of first-pass vein-hosted targeting — but the grades define the structural framework for follow-up drilling to test along-strike and at depth in an underexplored section of northwestern BC adjacent to historic high-grade producers.
